PullRequest.Title: explorer: coalesce parent refreshes during bulk moves
PullRequest.Body:

Fixes #339610.

Moving 32 files between expanded Explorer folders repeatedly refreshed the same parents. This coalesces **multi-file MOVE view refreshes** using the existing working-copy lifecycle, without deferring model mutations. Completion joins asynchronous handlers and the final refreshes, including undo/redo and partial failure.

**Review correction:** `cf33d529` preserves multi-source tree ownership by finishing source refreshes before final destination refreshes. The final-head rerun retains **229.8-231.7 ms** per-window move medians and **2 parent refreshes**. The original comparison and clips below remain pinned to `19ad8071`.

| Matched Windows fixture | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Expanded operation, median of 15 samples | 2,110.4 ms | **238.3 ms** |
| Exact painted tree, separate 5 samples | 3,100.9 ms | **333.1 ms** |
| Parent refreshes / tree passes through quiescence | 64 / 64 | **2 / 2** |

Three fresh windows pass the original one-second expectation. Additional checks verify exact disk/model/tree entries, painted completion, drag, undo/redo, cut/paste, expansion, and selection/focus. No timer, collapse, setting, or whole-tree refresh is added. Collapsed-parent timings are diagnostic controls, never fixed-experience results.

Four-second original UI excerpts, with startup removed and the completed frame held. This is asynchronous latency, not a renderer-blocking or memory claim.

<details>
<summary>Multi-source review regression and final-head verification</summary>

The review was reproduced in the real workbench: after Ctrl-selecting `a/x.txt` and `b/y.txt` and dragging to expanded `c`, both files existed under `c`, but `tree.hasNode(y)` was false. Four real-tree file/folder cases also failed at the previous PR head; the two chain controls passed.

The fix completes the source-parent phase before the final destination phase. A parent serving both roles participates in both phases. Destination refreshes are still attempted if a source refresh fails, and the error remains propagated.

All six real `WorkbenchCompressibleAsyncDataTree` cases now pass: shared destination, chained parents and exchanged files/folders, including descendant lookup, reveal, focus and selection. The unchanged live scenario passes for both files, moved folders and their children, followed by a new child update without a manual refresh.

Final head: `cf33d529444822398262b7a5593f9e841b8981eb`.
[Portable review repro and raw verification](https://github.com/karthiknadig/vscode/tree/c51310887926c6ee8e6a509b4284defc12604bf4/perf-swarm-wave4-explorer-bulk-move/multi-source-review).

| Validation | Result |
|---|---|
| `scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\files\test\browser\explorerService.test.ts --grep multi-source` on previous PR implementation | 4 expected failures; 2 controls passed |
| `scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\files\test\browser\explorerService.test.ts --run src\vs\base\test\browser\ui\tree\asyncDataTree.test.ts` | 49 passed |
| Original file-operation/Explorer/working-copy selection, exact command in linked verification | 162 passed, 1 existing skip; overlaps the ExplorerService tests above |
| `npm run typecheck-client`; changed-file ESLint and repository formatter | Passed |
| Original performance scenario, unchanged, `--isolation rev-explorer-perf --repeat 3` | 3/3 passed; expanded medians 229.8 / 231.7 / 231.4 ms |
| Original strict painted-state scenario, `--isolation rev-explorer-strict --repeat 1` | Passed; 302.1 ms painted median, 2 parent refreshes / 2 passes through each tree render method |
| New multi-source live scenario on previous/final implementation | Failed on the old lookup defect; passed all four steps after the correction |

These are separate final-head validation runs, not a claim that the original images were recorded again.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Root cause, lifecycle boundaries, and compatibility</summary>

The [per-file MOVE handler](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/24a41178148f72f49e4ac0756ddb3b5347429a91/src/vs/workbench/contrib/files/browser/explorerService.ts#L413) refreshed both parents for each file. Separate coverage confirms 64 parent refreshes and 64 logical tree passes for 32 moves. Repeated Explorer filtering/rendering is the verified cost; no independent claim is made about the generic intersecting-refresh queue.

The fix reuses [working-copy operation completion](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/24a41178148f72f49e4ac0756ddb3b5347429a91/src/vs/workbench/services/workingCopy/common/workingCopyFileService.ts#L413), which also wraps undo/redo. Correlation IDs isolate overlapping batches, URI identity matches actual move events, and refreshes are keyed by model item so overlapping workspace roots remain distinct. Recursive refresh requirements are merged, not downgraded.

The completion participant joins the asynchronous file-event handlers before flushing. Both success and failure flush completed mutations, every parent refresh is attempted, and pending state is released in `finally` or disposal. File-operation errors still propagate; event/view errors use the existing unexpected-error reporting channel.

Sixteen new tests cover immediate model changes, coalescing, asynchronous continuations, final-render completion, nested/concurrent and matching overlapping batches, late events, partial failure, actual bulk-edit cancellation boundaries, single-file responsiveness, case-insensitive URI identity, distinct same-URI model parents, folder descendants/rename/nesting, copy/delete/external changes, refresh failure, and disposal before/during flushing.

The actual UI run covers a 32-file drag, keyboard undo/redo and cut/paste. All current disk and model names and actual tree children are checked; rendered viewport entries are separately verified. Both parent folders stay expanded. Unmoved selection/focus is asserted; post-action selection/focus matches the baseline.

Scope: local Windows fixture, not a universal zero-regression claim. Copy/delete and external watcher paths are not batched. This does not close the external Python watcher report #165271 or make a cache/LRU, initial-expansion, or memory claim.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Measurements, controls, and exact executed validation</summary>

Baseline: `24a41178148f72f49e4ac0756ddb3b5347429a91`; fixed: `19ad8071e6989a74ab0697bf62c14ca9c0e9f2c8`. Code OSS 1.141.0 Dev / Electron 43.7.5, Windows x64. The fixture contains 1,024 ordinary local TS files totaling 23,552 bytes; each operation moves 32 between sibling folders.

Per revision: three fresh primary windows, one warmup plus five measured samples per expanded/collapsed arm. The stronger supplementary run uses one additional fresh window and one warmup plus five exact-painted samples. Profiled samples are excluded from timing medians. Counts extend through empty refresh queues, no pending file-event scheduler/backlog, and 600 ms of quiescence. Quiescent elapsed time includes the existing watcher delay and observation interval; it is not confused with visible completion.

[All controlled samples, controls, completion boundaries and counts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/karthiknadig/vscode/82f335c471525a4fc21dad8de15f7bc59daf5599/perf-swarm-wave4-explorer-bulk-move/metrics.json).

Commands below retain the executed arguments; `$repo`, `$proof`, and `$swarm` replace only machine-local checkout, evidence, and Bug Swarm installation prefixes. Every heavy command ran through `with-perf-lock.ps1 -Owner w4-explorer-fix -FilePath <executable> -ArgumentList <arguments>`. Owned windows closed before releasing the lease.

The original scenario's input and one-second assertion are unchanged. A source-row readiness wait was added identically to both copies after a setup race, and both revisions were rerun. The supplementary drag's viewport setup was likewise repaired on both sides without weakening any state/timing assertion.

Not run: installed Insiders (pending update left untouched), macOS/Linux, remote providers, or a screen reader. CI and human review remain separate from these local results.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Portable reproduction and manual checks</summary>

Download the [primary scenario](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/karthiknadig/vscode/82f335c471525a4fc21dad8de15f7bc59daf5599/perf-swarm-wave4-explorer-bulk-move/bulk-move-scenario.cjs) and [supplementary scenario](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/karthiknadig/vscode/82f335c471525a4fc21dad8de15f7bc59daf5599/perf-swarm-wave4-explorer-bulk-move/supplementary.cjs) into the same folder. They create disposable synthetic workspaces and never use repository files as inputs.

From a built checkout, the standard scenario runner can reproduce the primary case:

```powershell
node test\scenario\out\runScenario.js --dev <downloaded-folder>\bulk-move-scenario.cjs
```

The primary scenario uses platform-neutral path handling; the supplementary keyboard gestures are Windows-specific. Only Windows was executed. To reproduce the isolated validation above, use Bug Swarm's `run-scenario.mjs` with `--checkout <checkout> --isolation <unique-name> --repeat 3`. Do not overlap performance runs.

Manual check: open a folder with 1,024 small files in `source` and an empty sibling `destination`. Keep the parents expanded, select 32 source files, and drag them to the destination. Check the resulting entries, undo, redo, then cut/paste them back. The final names and expansion should remain correct without seconds of repeated updates.

</details>

<sub>Found and fixed by Bug Swarm. Draft, assigned to karthiknadig, for human review.</sub>

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Each item in a bulk move independently refreshed both expanded Explorer parents, repeatedly filtering, sorting, diffing, and rendering the same child collections; for N sibling files this caused 2N tree update passes instead of two parent reconciliations.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Bulk moves between expanded Explorer folders incurred latency growing linearly with the number of selected files because the same source and destination trees were reconciled once per file.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The changed refreshMove path records refresh requirements in a Map keyed by ExplorerItem (line 457), merges recursive requirements, and finishMoveBatch flushes each unique source parent once before each unique target parent once at working-copy operation completion. Cost now scales with unique affected parents rather than moved files.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: In the base revision, every synchronous FileService MOVE event enters ExplorerService.onDidRunOperation and the line at base 453 invokes view.refresh(false, oldParent) inside the per-moved-item handler; the adjacent target refresh does the same for the destination. ExplorerView.refresh delegates to tree.updateChildren, so moving N items between two expanded parents launches 2N collection-wide tree reconciliation passes. The added 32-item test directly establishes the changed cardinality: model mutations still happen for all 32 events while refreshes are deferred and reduced to exactly one source plus one target refresh.

Scenarios.Scenario: Moving many selected files between expanded Explorer folders by drag/drop or cut/paste
Scenarios.CriticalPath: BulkFileEdits awaits IWorkingCopyFileService.move; after the existing per-file filesystem moves complete, the changed working-copy completion participant now waits for Explorer model handlers and one coalesced source-parent phase followed by one target-parent phase before the command/progress completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Validate, move, and resolve each source/target pair through IFileService.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: For N selected entries, N canMove validations and N sequential move operations; each move also resolves its target metadata. Remote providers may implement these as remote filesystem traffic.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical per-file validation/move/resolve cardinality and serialization.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All N operations were and remain on the bulk-move critical path before Explorer completion handling.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Reconcile affected Explorer tree children through tree.updateChildren.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One pass per unique source parent and one per unique target parent after identity-based coalescing; two passes for N sibling files moved between two expanded folders, versus two passes per file before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same boundary ran once for each source and destination parent on every FileService MOVE event, yielding 2N passes for the common case.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The final coalesced passes are now joined to working-copy completion; although this places two passes on command completion, it replaces 2N asynchronously launched passes whose repeated filtering/diffing/rendering dominated visible completion.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N selected files and P unique affected model parents after URI/model identity matching. Filesystem work remains O(N); Explorer reconciliation changes from O(N) repeated passes over the same parent collections to O(P), with P=2 in the primary sibling-folder workflow.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: File validation and filesystem moves remain sequential in WorkingCopyFileService. FileService events synchronously launch model handlers. Final refreshes run concurrently only across distinct source parents, then concurrently across distinct target parents; for the common one-source/one-target case this is one refresh in each phase. This is lower aggregate tree concurrency than the pre-diff per-event launches.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Expanded parents have resolved ExplorerItem children, so updateChildren consumes the warm model and does not add filesystem resolves. Parent requirements are transiently coalesced by ExplorerItem identity and recursive flags are merged. If the view is hidden or the node is absent, ExplorerView.refresh resolves without tree work. Batch maps are cleared on success, failure, and disposal.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed lines record refreshes in a per-batch Map, tests establish 32 immediate model mutations and exactly two final refreshes, and ExplorerView.refresh directly calls tree.updateChildren.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact tree-pass cost varies with parent size, nesting/filter settings, filesystem provider, and visibility, but the before/after multiplicity is directly established by the changed handler and tests.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The PR removes repeated collection-wide rendering work; the bounded completion join preserves final ordering and has lower total and peak tree work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Undo/redo and overlapping or multi-source bulk moves
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Undo and redo reuse IWorkingCopyFileService.move and therefore enter the same correlation-scoped batching path. Completion waits for matching model continuations, then reconciles all unique source parents before all unique destination parents.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Perform reverse or repeated move operations for undo/redo.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: N sequential filesystem moves per undo or redo operation, unchanged by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Undo/redo used the same per-file filesystem operations and generated per-file Explorer events.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Filesystem work remains the dominant mandatory operation and precedes completion refreshes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Update unique source model parents first, then unique target model parents.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one refresh per ExplorerItem per role/phase for each correlation-scoped batch; a parent serving both roles may correctly participate in both phases.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Every item event immediately launched source and target refreshes without per-operation coalescing or phase ordering.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Flushes are joined to each operation's completion so subsequent undo/redo state observes a reconciled tree.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N moved entries, P unique source/target ExplorerItem parents, and B concurrently active operations. Event matching is O(N*B), but B is normally one and overlapping operations are short-lived; rendering is O(P) per batch rather than O(N).
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each working-copy move operation has an independent correlation ID. Matching FileService events can join overlapping batches, while each batch flushes independently. Within a flush, distinct parents are parallelized by phase; source and target phases remain ordered. The pre-diff implementation launched more concurrent refresh promises, one set per item event.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Correlation IDs isolate batches; source-to-target URI maps only match actual events, and refresh maps retain state only for operation lifetime. Cleanup runs in finally and disposal clears all pending maps. Overlapping batches do not share cached refresh state and therefore do not create stale cross-operation entries.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: event correlations, matching loop, phased Promise settlement, overlapping-batch tests, and disposal tests all establish ownership and bounded lifetime.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The prevalence of truly overlapping user operations and number of workspace-root aliases is low and not measured, but lifecycle and multiplicity are directly visible.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. No new unbounded concurrency or retention was found; phase-parallel work is bounded by unique parents and replaces a larger pre-existing refresh burst.

Scenarios.Scenario: Partial failure, cancellation, single-file rename/move, and non-move file changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Multi-file MOVE failures invoke the same completion flush for model mutations that already occurred. Single-file moves do not create a batch and continue to refresh immediately. Copy, delete, create, and external watcher paths bypass move batching.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Attempt moves until the first filesystem failure or complete the single operation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to N sequential move attempts for a multi-file operation; one for single-file moves. Unchanged by this diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same filesystem attempts occurred; successful prefixes each launched immediate source/target tree refreshes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Failure notification waits for cleanup participants, including only the coalesced refreshes for mutations that fired events.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Settle successful model handlers and flush unique affected parents on success or failure.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One refresh per unique affected parent for the successful prefix; zero for an empty failed batch. Single-file moves retain immediate parent refreshes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Successful-prefix events launched refreshes per file and completion did not join them.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only multi-file MOVE completion/failure joins the coalesced tree work. Non-move and single-file paths are not delayed by batch state.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: K successful moves before failure and P unique affected parents. Final rendering scales with P rather than K; single-item behavior remains constant.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Partial successes are processed sequentially by WorkingCopyFileService and their collected refreshes are settled before the failure event completes. Single-file and non-move events preserve the prior immediate async-handler behavior.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Empty and partially filled batches are deleted before flushing and all transient maps/arrays/sets are cleared in finally. Late unmatched events take the immediate path. There is no negative cache or persistent retained-key growth.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: didRun/didFail share finishMoveBatch, deletion precedes awaits, finally clears retained state, and tests cover empty failure, partial failure, late events, and disposal.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider-specific failure timing varies, but bounded cleanup and late-event behavior are covered by direct tests.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. Cleanup is bounded on all represented lifecycle exits and unrelated operation classes remain outside the batching path.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all changed files and diff pages. The production change replaces per-file Explorer tree refreshes with correlation-scoped, identity-keyed parent coalescing and bounded cleanup. Transitive filesystem cardinality is unchanged, tree-update cardinality drops from per moved item to per unique affected parent, and no actionable diff-introduced latency, fan-out, concurrency, cache, or retention regression was found. Recorded the concrete repeated-work regression fix against its introducing base commit.
